items.title: Using AI To Make Patches For The Yamaha CS-80 Synthesizer
items.excerpt: A Jose's Vintage Keys video shows Anthropic's Claude programming patches on a MIDI-modded Yamaha CS-80, turning text descriptions into sound-design starting points on vintage hardware.

items.title: ‘Suno is the new auto-tune’: Meet the artists using AI to go viral
items.excerpt: Dazed profiles masked TikTok-viral acts such as Kilo Kent and Zemi who sing their own songs and run the vocals through Suno like a studio effect, arguing the songwriting stays theirs. (Off-list: no allowed-domain outlet covered this creator-workflow angle.)

items.title: Tencent Music’s MusicBuddy combines AI music creation, editing, distribution and promotion
items.excerpt: Tencent Music is testing MusicBuddy, an AI platform that pairs song generation with a multitrack editor driven by natural-language chat, then pushes tracks to release and promotion. (Off-list: tool release not covered by allowed domains.)

items.title: Instagram adds AI songs to DMs
items.excerpt: Instagram is testing a Meta AI song-creation option in the DM inbox: users add lyrics and pick a genre to generate a track to send to friends, echoing Snapchat's paid Chat-to-Song. (Off-list: feature release not covered by allowed domains.)

items.title: Lalu's Corner: Who Controls the Digital Version of You?
items.excerpt: A column on artist likeness in the AI era: the Jason Isbell suit alleging Suno's name block is bypassed by spacing letters, a deadmau5 deepfake endorsement, and the Jorja Smith soundalike, plus how labels split between licensing and takedowns.

items.title: Audiotool reveals six winners from its ‘Let’s Build!’ hackathon
items.excerpt: Audiotool's music-app hackathon winners include Pocket Producer, an AI agent for music producers, and an AI A&R Assistant that analyses tracks and estimates earning potential, alongside DAW-conversion and sheet-music tools.

items.title: Olivia Rodrigo Clarifies AI Stance Following ‘Invasive’ Tech Investor Dating Rumors: ‘Absolutely No’
items.excerpt: Olivia Rodrigo says she has 'absolutely no' plans to use AI in her music, addressing rumours that tied her to an AI tech investor.

items.title: DistroKid Takedown Wave Hits Indie Artists After UMG Lawsuit
items.excerpt: With UMG's lawsuit over AI 'slop' uploads pending, DistroKid is aggressively purging tracks, and artists say their legitimate releases are caught in the crossfire. (Follow-up to the Verge DistroKid story published 10-11.)

items.title: “In the beginning we often called our studio an electronic garden – but that garden developed into a factory farming industry”: Kraftwerk’s Karl Bartos tells us how technology curbed the band’s creativity
items.excerpt: Ex-Kraftwerk member Karl Bartos calls AI in music 'overestimated... just an archive of human logic' and a Silicon Valley sales pitch, in an interview on studio technology and his Caligari score. (AI is one segment of a broader interview.)

items.title: “We will keep enforcing our artists’ rights... but it’s becoming an uphill struggle”: Sony Music reveals the number of deepfake AI tracks it’s asked to be removed has doubled in six months
items.excerpt: Sony Music says its AI deepfake takedown requests have doubled in six months to over 260,000, and its president estimates up to 10% of streams could be fraudulent. (Same story as MBW piece published 10-06; check for dup.)

items.title: LiveSynth: A Streaming Neural Synthesizer for Instrument Cloning and Text-to-Instrument
items.excerpt: LiveSynth is a streaming neural synthesizer that clones an instrument's timbre zero-shot from a reference recording or generates one from a text prompt, and plays in real time rather than rendering audio offline.

items.title: MIRA: A Musical Intent Refinement Agent for Aligning Text-to-Music Generation with User Intent
items.excerpt: MIRA is an agent that refines underspecified text-to-music prompts toward the user's implicit intent on instrumentation, structure, rhythm and mood, instead of relying on a single global text-audio relevance score.
